summary: Proposes changing the link function of the TENEX operating system to give a better user interface. The author says BBN had no complaints about the current version, asks for quick feedback, and promises to share the new version once tried.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 576 proposes a TENEX linking change that lets people in an existing conversation control whether another user can join. It also proposes a system call for checking which terminals are linked or advising one another.

questions: how did tenex users join a conversation
what does refuse links mean in rfc 576
subtitle: A proposed change to how TENEX users join linked conversations.

tldr.problem: The author proposed changing TENEX linking to improve its user interface for conversations among multiple users.
tldr.mechanism: After users link, the proposal places conversation members in REFUSE LINKS state. A new link attempt rings a bell; accepting links during that alert adds the requester to the conversation.
tldr.outcome: The proposal also calls for a system call to report link and advise status and requests feedback before implementation.

today: RFC 576 is a proposal describing a possible change to TENEX linking behavior.

sections.title: The Proposed Linking Behavior
sections.content:
The proposal leaves the default user state as RECEIVE LINKS. When two users link to each other, they form a conversation and all its members enter REFUSE LINKS. A later user who tries to link causes a bell to ring on the relevant terminals.

If the alerted user does not act, the requester is not admitted and the existing conversation continues. If a participant uses RECEIVE LINKS while the bell is ringing, the requester joins the conversation rather than linking only to that participant.
sections.plainLanguage: Two users can link and then refuse new links by default. If another user asks to join, a participant can accept the request while the bell rings.

sections.title: Leaving a Conversation
sections.content: When a user leaves a conversation, the proposal automatically places that user in RECEIVE LINKS state. If one member leaves a three-person conversation, the remaining members stay linked and remain in REFUSE LINKS. When a participant breaks the link in a two-person conversation, the other participant is also left without a conversation and returns to RECEIVE LINKS.
sections.plainLanguage: A person who leaves a conversation becomes ready to receive links again. The remaining participants keep their conversation and continue refusing new links.

sections.title: System Changes and Status Information
sections.content:
The proposal says changes to the TLINK JSYS are needed, but no EXEC changes are required. It also proposes a new JSYS that reports link and advise relationships for a terminal. The author says this information might be included in status displays and might be used by NLS for shared-screen work.

The author requests feedback over the next couple of days before deciding whether to implement this proposal, a modified one or nothing.
sections.plainLanguage: The change would update TLINK and add a way for programs to inspect link relationships. At the time of the note, the author was still asking for feedback before deciding what to implement.
